identity.title: ALMA observations of the variability of the quiet Sun at millimeter wavelengths

paper_type_evidence.quote: We used Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the quiet Sun at 1.26 mm and 3 mm.

evidence.quote: it was centered at heliocentric coordinates of about -132$''$, -398$''$ ($\mu \approx 0.9$).

question.value: Variability of the quiet solar chromosphere at 1.26 mm and 3 mm: spatially resolved p-mode oscillations and transient brightenings

evidence.quote: We address the variability of the quiet solar chromosphere at 1.26 mm and 3 mm with a focus on the study of spatially resolved oscillations and transient brightenings

bands.value: Band 6 (1.26 mm, 239 GHz) and Band 3 (3 mm, 100 GHz)

evidence.quote: Band 6 at 1.26 mm (239 GHz)
spatial resolution of 1.6$''$ by 0.7$''$ for Band 6 and 2.7$''$ by 1.7$''$ for Band 3

time_on_source.value: Band 6: 8 scans (6 of ~7.9 min, 2 of ~2 min); Band 3: 6 scans (4 of ~9.9 min, 2 of ~6.9 min)

evidence.quote: Each scan had a duration of about 7.9 min, with the exception of scans 4 and 8 which had a duration of about 2 min.
Our observations took place on 12 April 2018

provided.value: 1600 and 304 A images for pointing correction and event comparison

evidence.quote: comparison with simultaneous 1600 Å data taken with the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA; Lemen et al. 2012)
Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) aboard SDO magnetograms
single frames of the best nearest H$\alpha$ images from the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG)

method.value: Cross-correlate ALMA images with AIA 1600 A; re-compute average and 1 s snapshot CLEAN images with self-calibration; combine with full-disk images

evidence.quote: We computed the actual pointing by cross-correlating the ALMA images with the 1600 Å images

validation.value: Offset consistent with general-relativistic radial offset

evidence.quote: verified that the position offset we established was consistent with the general-relativistic radial offset

method.value: Per-pixel light curves in blocks (scans 1-4, 5-8; 1-3, 4-6), zero-filled gaps, FT to PSD, averaged over 120x120 pixel FoV and blocks; fit log-normal plus linear in ln(nu)

evidence.quote: zeroes were added to fill the blanks in the concatenated light curves.

key_parameters.value: Fit range lower 2-4 mHz, upper 30-50 mHz chosen by minimum chi^2

evidence.quote: The lower and upper frequency employed in our analysis was the one leading to the smallest ${\chi}^{2}$.

fitting.value: chi^2 minimization of PSD model a0+a1 ln nu+a2 exp(...)

evidence.quote: for each combination of lower and upper frequency that could be drawn from these intervals, we performed the PSD fitting and calculated the corresponding ${\chi}^{2}$.

evidence.quote: relatively small absolute residuals (blue solid lines) not exceeding $\approx 20 \%$.

method.value: Remove oscillations, then require >=4 consecutive points above 2.5 sigma, shared by a beam-size patch of 18 pixels, peaking within +-2 min; same on AIA 304/1600 with 1 point

evidence.quote: at least four consecutive points in each “corrected” time profile should have intensity exceeding a 2.5$\sigma$ threshold above the mean intensity of the light curve

findings_qualitative.value: Bright ALMA network structures correspond to dark mottles/spicules in broadband H-alpha

evidence.quote: We also found that ALMA bright network structures corresponded to dark mottles/spicules seen in broadband H$\alpha$ images from the GONG network.

claims.hypothesis: p-mode relative amplitude is similar at 1.26 and 3 mm when matched for resolution and FoV
claims.finding: Relative amplitude does not change appreciably between formation heights

evidence.quote: These results imply that the p-mode relative amplitude does not appreciably change between the formation heights of the 1.26 mm and 3 mm emissions.

claims.hypothesis: Weaker, lower-energy events can be detected at 1.26 mm
claims.result: Energies 1.8e23-1.1e26 erg at 1.26 mm; occurrence rate higher than at 3 mm
claims.finding: 1.26 mm low-end energies are among the smallest reported

evidence.quote: Even lower was the lower end of the energy distribution of the 1.26 mm events, which is among the smallest ever reported

limitations_admitted.value: Observed p-mode rms is a lower limit since resolution is coarse and pixels are correlated
